'''William Hamilton Meeks, III''' (August 8, 1947 - May 24, 2026) was an [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]], specializing in [[differential geometry]] and [[minimal surface]]s.

== Biography ==
Meeks studied at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], with a [[bachelor's degree]] in 1971, a [[master's degree]] in 1974, and a [[PhD]] in 1975 with supervisor [[H. Blaine Lawson]] and thesis ''The Conformal Structure and Geometry of Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces in <math> \mathbb R ^ 3 </math>''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 32068}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=The conformal structure and geometry of triply periodic minimal surfaces in <math>R^3</math>|author=Meeks III, William H.|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=83|year=1977|pages=134–136|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1977-14218-3|doi-access=free}} (published version of 1975 Berkeley Ph.D. thesis)</ref> He was an assistant professor in 1975–1977 at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), in  1977–1978 at the [[Instituto de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]] (IMPA), and in 1978–1979 at [[Stanford University]]. From 1979 to 1983 he was a professor at IMPA. He was from 1983 to 1984 a visiting member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and from 1984 to 1986 a professor at [[Rice University]] with the academic year 1985–1986 spent as a visiting professor at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. From 1986 to 2018 he was the George David Birkhoff Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Massachusetts, Amherst]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|url=http://people.math.umass.edu/~bill/papers/billentirecv.pdf|title=William Hamilton Meeks, III, C.V.|date=29 April 2008|website=math.umass.edu}}</ref> Later, he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] after assuming professor emeritus status at UMass Amherst.<ref>{{cite web |title=William H. Meeks |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/william-h-meeks |website=Members of the Institute for Advanced Study |publisher=Institute for Advanced Study |accessdate=11 September 2018}}</ref>

He was known as an expert on minimal surfaces and their computer graphics visualization; on the latter subject he collaborated with [[David Allen Hoffman]]. For the academic year 2006/07 Meeks was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]].<ref name=CV/>

In 1986 at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], he was Invited Speaker with talk ''Recent progress on the geometry of surfaces in <math> R ^ 3 </math> and on the use of computer graphics as a research tool''.<ref name=CV/>
